claude.take: This is a read, not a recommendation. NSE is the highest-quality asset to come to an Indian IPO in years on almost every operating measure — 92.99% cash-market share, 99.79% equity futures, zero debt, ~51% PAT margin, ₹7,949 Cr of operating cash flow, ₹34,600 Cr of treasury, ₹8,662 Cr of dividends paid in FY26. It is also the only way to own Indian exchange infrastructure at scale, and the anchor book — 189 investors, LIC largest and choosing to buy rather than sell — says serious institutions are comfortable at ₹1,785. The relative-value case is real: BSE trades at ~54x for a much smaller business while NSE is being offered at ~43x. That is the entire bull thesis and it is not a weak one. The other side is equally concrete. FY26 was a down year on both revenue and profit, and the ~43x is being paid on that declining base. Options are 60.22% of operating revenue and NSE's share of that segment has gone 96.9% → 74.71% → 68.5% in roughly two years, on the revenue-densest part of the business; the multiple only works if that curve flattens, which it has not yet. 78.65% of operating revenue sits on transaction charges that a single SEBI circular can reprice, and SEBI has done exactly that once already. The co-location and dark-fibre matters are proposed-settled at ₹1,491 Cr but not closed. Nothing of the ₹22,562 Cr reaches the company. And the market's own pricing signals are softening, not firming: GMP down from ₹285 to ₹160, the band set ~10% below the ₹1,990 unlisted quote and ~26% below the ₹2,400 unlisted peak, Day-1 morning book at 0.13x. Both statements are true at once — a great business, priced for a recovery that has not yet shown up in the numbers. Which of those two facts matters more depends entirely on holding period, and that is a judgement each investor has to make for themselves.

recs.consensus: Skewed positive but not unanimous, and the positives are relative rather than absolute. Choice Broking, Ventura, Swastika and Angel One are all at SUBSCRIBE; Religare Broking is NEUTRAL. Dilip Davda (Chittorgarh/IPO Watch) calls it 'fully priced' and says well-informed investors can park funds for medium-to-long-term rewards — which is a park-it call, not a listing-pop call. Value Research is the most sceptical, framing 48x FY26 against ~6% profit growth as a valuation that already assumes the options market-share bleed stops. The recurring pro-argument across houses is the same one: NSE at ~42.9x is cheaper than BSE at ~54.3x despite being the far larger and structurally stronger exchange, and there is no substitute asset. The recurring counter-argument is also the same: ~79% of revenue is transaction-linked and SEBI has already shown it can reprice that overnight.

company.about: India's largest stock exchange and, by number of contracts traded, the largest derivatives exchange in the world. NSE operates the cash equity, equity derivatives, currency, commodity and debt segments, along with clearing (NSE Clearing), market data, connectivity/co-location and index licensing (Nifty family). It held 92.99% of Indian cash-market turnover, 99.79% of equity futures and 74.71% of equity options in FY26. The registered investor base grew from 3.087 crore in March 2020 to 13.237 crore by June 2026, a 26.23% CAGR, and ₹20.33 lakh crore of capital was mobilised on its platforms in FY26. The company has no identifiable promoter under SECC Regulations and is professionally managed.

demand.read: Two readings sit on top of each other. The anchor book is about as good as an Indian anchor book gets — 189 investors, LIC as the largest, every major domestic fund house plus GIC, ADIA, Norges and Fidelity — and at ₹6,746 Cr it is itself larger than most Indian IPOs. That is genuine institutional validation of the price. But the public book on Day 1 morning is slow: 0.13x overall at 10:50, retail 0.17x, NII 0.22x, employee the most enthusiastic category. That is not alarming for a ₹22,562 Cr issue on a three-day book where QIB and NII money typically arrives on the last day, and the absolute rupee demand at 0.13x is already larger than most whole IPOs. Still, retail running behind NII at this stage, on the most famous name in Indian capital markets, is worth noting: the ticket is only ₹14,280, so lack of affordability is not the explanation. GMP has faded from ₹285 on 7 Sep to ₹160 today, and the ₹1,785 band prices roughly 10% below the recent ₹1,990 unlisted-market quote and ~26% below the June 2025 unlisted peak of ₹2,400 — which means unlisted holders who bought near the top are underwater at the IPO price, a known source of supply on listing.

financials.read: Total income (₹Cr) and PAT (₹Cr). FY26 is the first down year in the set on both lines — income −2.4% and PAT −15.5% — and that is the central fact of this IPO. The cause is regulatory, not operational: SEBI's 2024-25 derivatives measures (weekly expiry limits, higher lot sizes) cut index options volumes, and options are 60.22% of operating revenue while transaction charges overall are 78.65%. Options market share has fallen from 96.9% in FY24 to 74.71% in FY26 and 68.5% in Q1 FY27. Underneath, the business quality is extraordinary: PAT margin ~51%, EBITDA-level margins around 65%, zero borrowings, ₹7,949 Cr operating cash flow in FY26, ₹34,600 Cr of own treasury, and ₹8,662 Cr paid out as dividends in FY26. Note also that FY25 contained one-off gains, which makes the FY26 decline look worse than the underlying trend — and equally makes FY25 a flattering base that nobody should annualise from. Some trackers report slightly different FY25/FY26 PAT (₹11,606 Cr / ₹10,180 Cr); the RHP-based consolidated figures above are the ones used here.

valuation.read: At ₹1,785 the issue values NSE at about ₹4,41,787 Cr on FY26 diluted EPS of ₹41.62 — roughly 42.9x, with published estimates spanning 40.9x to 48x depending on whether FY26 or a trailing/annualised base is used. P/B is 13.76x on NAV of ₹129.75 and RoNW is 33.21%. The bull framing is relative: the only listed comparable, BSE, trades at 54.28x on a business a fraction of NSE's size, so the larger and structurally stronger exchange is being offered at a discount to the smaller one rather than at a premium. Dilip Davda's arithmetic puts it at 35.38x on annualised FY27 earnings, which is where the 'reasonable' case lives. The bear framing is absolute: 42.9x is a growth multiple, and FY26 earnings went backwards — PAT fell from ₹12,187.69 Cr to ₹10,302.06 Cr. Value Research puts the multiple at 48x FY26 against ~6% profit growth versus a decade-long ~30% average, and Religare says the price 'leaves limited room for earnings disappointments'. The whole multiple rests on options volumes recovering and market share stabilising; neither has happened yet.
